errors.english: Because if the certainty of being of that nature [note: essential identity] and arising from that [note: causality] follows it
errors.why: It is the conveying capacity that follows (rjes su 'jug) the certainty of tādātmya/tadutpatti, not the certainty that follows it.

note: Sound rendering of a dense Pramāṇa commentary; one inverted dependency, otherwise the argument is followed.

errors.english: although the object of sound does not have a nature of various conjunctions
errors.why: sgra'i yul is the referent of the word ('variegated'), i.e. although what the word denotes is not a variegated conjunction; not 'the object of sound'.

errors.english: the metaphor exists because of the "inherence" [note: original: "samavaya"] of many things into a single object of conjunction
errors.why: The Tibetan says conjunction inheres in a single object (ekārthasamavāya), not that many things inhere in an object of conjunction.

note: Generally accurate account of the citra-buddhi / saṃyoga argument, with two Vaiśeṣika technicalities blurred.

errors.english: She spoke thus to him, and the merchant's daughter replied: "Noble son, he will teach me
errors.why: Sadāprarudita answers the merchant's daughter, addressing her as 'girl' (bu mo); the English makes the daughter the speaker of his reply.

fix.find: She spoke thus to him, and the merchant's daughter replied: "Noble son, he will teach me
fix.replace: He replied to her: "Girl, that noble son will teach me

errors.english: all this should be applied extensively."
errors.why: The commentator's abbreviation instruction ('supply the passage in full up to …') is placed inside the daughter's quoted speech.

note: Readable rendering of the Sadāprarudita episode, but the speaker of the key reply is misassigned and the commentator's ellipsis markers are absorbed into the narrative.

errors.english: transforming the mental continuum [note: original: "rgyud," referring to the stream of consciousness]
errors.why: In this mantra argument the continuum transformed is that of the mantra (its successive moments), not the practitioner's stream of consciousness.

errors.english: rather, the mantras are unmanifest
errors.why: The clause says the application does not produce mantras but rather [manifests] mantras that are unmanifest, which leads into the refuted manifestation view.

note: Faithful overall to the anti-Mīmāṃsā mantra argument; minor slips in the gloss and one clause.

errors.english: are viable [note: literally: "fit for a youth to eat"] and undamaged
errors.why: khye'u kha 'thon pa means 'capable of sprouting' (khye'u = sprout); the note invents a youth eating them.

fix.find: are viable [note: literally: "fit for a youth to eat"] and undamaged
fix.replace: are capable of sprouting, not made allowable, and undamaged

errors.english: are viable [note: literally: "fit for a youth to eat"] and undamaged
errors.why: The Vinaya condition 'not made allowable' (akalpīkṛta) is left out of the definition of the offence.

note: Accurate on the plant lists and pāyattika definition, but the offence condition is distorted by a wrong note and a dropped technical term.

errors.english: means that if the nature of what is claimed to be the nature of pervasiveness and so forth is also a separate entity—if this were not the case
errors.why: The Tibetan asserts the consequence (its nature too would have to be another object; otherwise …), not a conditional left hanging.

errors.english: it refers to things like a palace or a garland
errors.why: The stock example is a single compound, 'a row of mansions', not a palace and a garland.

errors.english: it is impossible for them to possess number, because both number and "possession" are quality-entities
errors.why: ldan pa here is conjunction (saṃyoga): number and conjunction are both impossible for the six categories, as qualities residing only in substance.

note: Follows the Vaiśeṣika regress argument reasonably, with some blurred technical points.

errors.english: When it arises in men who wish for harm
errors.why: The anger arises in oneself and the ill-wishers rejoice when it does; it does not arise in them.

fix.find: When it arises in men who wish for harm
fix.replace: When it arises, those who wish one harm

errors.english: In that anger of a king who acts wrongly,
errors.why: rgyal po is vocative ('O king'); the anger is the one that leads to wrong conduct, not the anger of a wrongdoing king.

fix.find: In that anger of a king who acts wrongly,
fix.replace: O king, in that anger which makes one act wrongly,

errors.english: a bad reputation arises [note: original: "gtam ngan" — here implying the loss of a worldly, aggressive reputation in favor of peace]
errors.why: The verse contrasts with the next one: the angry man is shunned and ill-repute befalls him like the waning moon; the note rationalises an inverted reading.

note: The prose frame is fine, but the verses on anger misassign who is angry and who is addressed, and one stanza's sense is inverted.

errors.english: when it is stated that a part of the subject's property that is to be proven is pervaded
errors.why: The pakṣadharma (the reason) is pervaded BY one part of the pakṣa (the sādhya-dharma); the English makes the part the thing pervaded.

errors.english: Since these are of an all-present nature, such a distinction is impossible.
errors.why: The point is that anvaya/vyatireka hold across all instances and such all-presence is impossible for a particular (the dharmin); not that 'a distinction is impossible'.

errors.english: it is appropriate that the qualifier itself functions as the means of understanding
errors.why: khyad par bya ba is the qualificandum (viśeṣya), not the qualifier (khyad par byed pa, viśeṣaṇa).

note: Logic vocabulary mostly right, but the pervader/pervaded and qualifier/qualified relations are confused at key points.

errors.english: (Upali) the Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of monastic law replied, "They should be given."
errors.why: Upāli is the questioner and is addressed by name in the Buddha's answer ('Upāli, they should be given'); he is not the one replying.

fix.find: (Upali) the Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of monastic law replied, "They should be given."
fix.replace: The Buddha replied, "(Upali), they should be given."

errors.english: the son will not return as the master of the father's house
errors.why: The reason for accepting is that the expelled son does not cease to be an owner of his father's house.

fix.find: the son will not return as the master of the father's house
fix.replace: the son does not cease to be an owner of the father's house

note: Workable rendering of difficult Vinaya-sūtra commentary, but the root-text dialogue and the rationale for the expelled-son rule are misread.

errors.english: If you ask, "Why is it negated?" the response is,
errors.why: 'Because that [cognition] negates it' is part of the opponent's objection, not a question about why it is negated.

note: Good, careful rendering of the apoha discussion with one misparsed objection.
